scorecard.rationale: Taiwanese cinnamon leaf oil and purified linalool favored anxiety-like behavior in healthy mice without a measured open-field movement change. Authenticated Ceylon bark oils sometimes contain linalool, with variable relative compositions and no detection in one direct survey of bark and commercial products. Neither chiral identity nor a transfer dose from an ordinary serving of ground bark to the positive mouse exposure is established. Existing constituent and extract comparisons also include null behavior results. Human and Parkinson data provide no attributable ground cinnamon anxiety contrast. A verified ingredient relationship survives as context and the symptom direction stays open.
